ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On the horizontal ground to the left of a vertical wall, a cube $ABCD$ with side length $a$ and mass $M$ is placed. Between the wall and the cube, a smooth ball with radius $R$ and mass $m$ is placed. Both the cube and the ball remain stationary, as shown in the figure. The center of the ball is $O$, and the angle between $OB$ and the vertical direction is $\theta$. The side length of the cube $a > R$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the cube and the horizontal ground is $\mu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$. It is assumed that the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction, and $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What are the magnitudes of the support forces $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ exerted by the cube and the wall on the ball?
2. If $\theta=45^{\circ}$, keeping the radius of the sphere unchanged and only increasing the mass of the sphere, what is the maximum mass of the sphere to prevent the cube from sliding? ($\tan45^{\circ}=1$)

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, cube ABCD is placed on horizontal ground, and there is a vertical wall on the right side. The small ball is located between the upper right corner B of the cube and the vertical wall, and simultaneously contacts the wall and point B of the cube. The center of the ball is O; OB is drawn in the figure, and the angle between OB and the vertical dashed-line direction is θ; the contact point between the ball and the wall is on the right side of the ball. The contacts are all smooth, so the supporting force of the wall on the ball is horizontally to the left, and the supporting force of the cube on the ball at point B is along the BO direction. Reasoning: Analyze the forces on the small ball. The small ball is subjected to gravity mg vertically downward, the supporting force N1 of the cube on the ball along the BO direction, and the supporting force N2 of the wall on the ball horizontally to the left. Since the angle between OB and the vertical direction is θ, the vertical component of N1 is N1 cosθ, and the horizontal component is N1 sinθ. The small ball is at rest, so in the vertical direction there is N1 cosθ = mg, and in the horizontal direction there is N2 = N1 sinθ. Solving gives N1 = mg/cosθ, N2 = mg tanθ. When θ = 45°, the force of the ball on the cube and the force of the cube on the ball are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Because tan45° = 1, the horizontal component of the ball on the cube is mg, and the vertically downward component is also mg. Therefore the supporting force of the ground on the cube is (M + m)g, and the magnitude of the static friction force required by the cube is mg. In order not to slide, mg ≤ μ(M + m)g is needed. Substituting μ = √3/3 gives m ≤ μ(M + m), that is, m(1 - μ) ≤ μM, so m_max = μM/(1 - μ) = (√3 + 1)M/2.

On the horizontal ground to the left of a vertical wall, a cube $ABCD$ with side length $a$ and mass $M$ is placed. Between the wall and the cube, a smooth ball with radius $R$ and mass $m$ is placed. Both the cube and the ball remain stationary, as shown in the figure. It is assumed that the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction, and $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What are the magnitudes of the support forces $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ exerted by the cube and the wall on the ball?
2. If $\theta=45^{\circ}$, keeping the radius of the sphere unchanged and only increasing the mass of the sphere, what is the maximum mass of the sphere to prevent the cube from sliding? ($\tan45^{\circ}=1$)

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the ball touches the vertical wall on its right and the cube at corner B; the line OB from the ball center to the contact point makes angle θ with the vertical, so the cube’s normal force on the ball is along OB, while the wall’s normal force is horizontal. Read from the text that all contacts involving the ball are smooth and the bodies are stationary. Draw separate free-body diagrams. For the ball, resolve forces into vertical and horizontal components: N1 cosθ balances mg, and N2 balances N1 sinθ, giving N1=mg/cosθ and N2=mg tanθ. For the cube when θ=45°, the ball pushes the cube oppositely along BO, with horizontal component mg and vertical component mg. Thus the ground normal on the cube is (M+m)g, and the required friction is mg. Use the limiting static-friction condition mg≤μ(M+m)g with μ=√3/3, then solve for the maximum m: m_max=((√3+1)/2)M.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中立方体 ABCD 放在水平地面上，右侧有竖直墙。小球位于立方体右上角 B 与竖直墙之间，并同时接触墙和立方体的 B 点。球心为 O，图中画出 OB，OB 与竖直虚线方向的夹角为 θ；球与墙的接触处在球的右侧。接触均光滑，因此墙对球的支持力水平向左，立方体在 B 点对球的支持力沿 BO 方向。

推理：对小球受力分析，小球受到重力 mg 竖直向下，立方体对球的支持力 N1 沿 BO 方向，墙对球的支持力 N2 水平向左。由于 OB 与竖直方向夹角为 θ，所以 N1 的竖直分量为 N1 cosθ，水平分量为 N1 sinθ。小球静止，因此竖直方向有 N1 cosθ = mg，水平方向有 N2 = N1 sinθ。解得 N1 = mg/cosθ，N2 = mg tanθ。

当 θ = 45° 时，球对立方体的作用力与立方体对球的作用力大小相等、方向相反。因为 tan45° = 1，所以球对立方体的水平分量为 mg，竖直向下分量也为 mg。因此地面对立方体的支持力为 (M + m)g，立方体所需的静摩擦力大小为 mg。为不滑动，需要 mg ≤ μ(M + m)g。代入 μ = √3/3，得到 m ≤ μ(M + m)，即 m(1 - μ) ≤ μM，所以 m_max = μM/(1 - μ) = (√3 + 1)M/2。
method.model_answer:
1. 立方体对球的支持力：N1 = mg/cosθ；墙对球的支持力：N2 = mg tanθ。
2. 当 θ = 45° 时，为防止立方体滑动，球的最大质量为 m_max = ((√3 + 1)/2)M。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the ball is a three-force body acted on by its weight, the horizontal wall reaction, and the oblique reaction from the cube along OB. Since the three forces are concurrent at O, construct a force triangle instead of writing component equations. From the triangle, the oblique cube reaction has vertical projection mg, so N1=mg/cosθ, and the horizontal wall reaction is N2=mg tanθ. For the second part, treat the cube plus ball as one combined system after obtaining N2. The internal contact force between cube and ball cancels. Externally, the wall pushes the system left with N2, the ground friction on the cube must push right with equal magnitude, and the ground normal balances the total weight (M+m)g. At θ=45°, N2=mg. Require mg≤μ(M+m)g and solve to get m_max=((√3+1)/2)M.

solver_metadata.cot_raw: 先描述图像：图中正方体放在水平地面上，右侧有竖直墙。光滑小球夹在正方体右上角附近和竖直墙之间；球心为 O，球与正方体接触点在 B 附近，OB 与竖直方向的夹角标为 θ，墙对球的支持力水平向左，正方体对球的支持力沿 OB 方向斜向上。再推理：小球是三力平衡物体，受重力 mg、墙的水平支持力 N2、正方体沿 OB 方向的支持力 N1。由力三角形可知，N1 的竖直分量平衡重力，所以 N1 cosθ = mg，得到 N1 = mg/cosθ；N1 的水平分量由墙的支持力平衡，所以 N2 = N1 sinθ = mg tanθ。第二问，当 θ = 45° 时，N2 = mg tan45° = mg。把正方体和小球看作整体，球与正方体间的接触力为内力而抵消；外力水平方向有墙对整体向左的 N2，地面对正方体的静摩擦力向右。为不滑动，需要 N2 ≤ fmax。整体竖直方向地面支持力平衡总重力，即 FN = (M + m)g，因此最大静摩擦力 fmax = μ(M + m)g。代入 μ = √3/3 且 N2 = mg，得 mg ≤ μ(M + m)g，即 m ≤ μ(M + m)。解得 m(1 - μ) ≤ μM，所以 mmax = μM/(1 - μ) = (√3 + 1)M/2。

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the cube contacts the ball at B, and OB is the radius to the contact point, inclined θ from the vertical; the wall reaction is perpendicular to the wall, so it is horizontal. Use the fact that for a smooth contact the reaction is normal to the surface/contact, hence along OB for the cube-ball contact. For the ball, require the resultant of weight mg and wall reaction N2 to be exactly opposite the cube reaction along OB. Therefore the resultant’s slope gives N2/mg=tanθ and the magnitude of the opposite force is N1=mg/cosθ. For the mass limit, use a friction-cone view at the cube-ground contact. At θ=45°, the ball’s force on the cube contributes a leftward horizontal load mg and an additional downward vertical load mg. The ground reaction on the cube must therefore have horizontal/vertical ratio mg/[(M+m)g]=m/(M+m). To avoid sliding this ratio must not exceed μ=√3/3. Solving m/(M+m)≤√3/3 gives m_max=((√3+1)/2)M.

raw_record.original_question:
On the horizontal ground to the left of a vertical wall, a cube $ABCD$ with side length $a$ and mass $M$ is placed. Between the wall and the cube, a smooth ball with radius $R$ and mass $m$ is placed. Both the cube and the ball remain stationary, as shown in the figure. The center of the ball is $O$, and the angle between $OB$ and the vertical direction is $\theta$. The side length of the cube $a > R$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the cube and the horizontal ground is $\mu = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$. It is assumed that the maximum static friction equals the sliding friction, and $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What are the magnitudes of the support forces $N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ exerted by the cube and the wall on the ball?
2. If $\theta=45^{\circ}$, keeping the radius of the sphere unchanged and only increasing the mass of the sphere, what is the maximum mass of the sphere to prevent the cube from sliding? ($\tan45^{\circ}=1$)
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, cube ABCD is placed on horizontal ground, and there is a vertical wall on the right side. The small ball is located between the upper right corner B of the cube and the vertical wall, and simultaneously contacts the wall and point B of the cube. The center of the ball is O; OB is drawn in the figure, and the angle between OB and the vertical dashed-line direction is θ; the contact point between the ball and the wall is on the right side of the ball. The contacts are all smooth, so the supporting force of the wall on the ball is horizontally to the left, and the supporting force of the cube on the ball at point B is along the BO direction.

Reasoning: Analyze the forces on the small ball. The small ball is subjected to gravity mg vertically downward, the supporting force N1 of the cube on the ball along the BO direction, and the supporting force N2 of the wall on the ball horizontally to the left. Since the angle between OB and the vertical direction is θ, the vertical component of N1 is N1 cosθ, and the horizontal component is N1 sinθ. The small ball is at rest, so in the vertical direction there is N1 cosθ = mg, and in the horizontal direction there is N2 = N1 sinθ. Solving gives N1 = mg/cosθ, N2 = mg tanθ.

When θ = 45°, the force of the ball on the cube and the force of the cube on the ball are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction. Because tan45° = 1, the horizontal component of the ball on the cube is mg, and the vertically downward component is also mg. Therefore the supporting force of the ground on the cube is (M + m)g, and the magnitude of the static friction force required by the cube is mg. In order not to slide, mg ≤ μ(M + m)g is needed. Substituting μ = √3/3 gives m ≤ μ(M + m), that is, m(1 - μ) ≤ μM, so m_max = μM/(1 - μ) = (√3 + 1)M/2.
